screening.title: How income ideas are screened here
screening.note: These are general considerations, not a religious ruling. Scholars differ on edge cases, and anything genuinely borderline is worth asking a qualified scholar about — especially around client sectors and contract structure.
avoid: Interest-based products and financing — designing sales material for interest-bearing loans, credit cards or conventional insurance, and funding your own business with an interest-bearing loan
Gambling, alcohol, pork, tobacco, adult content, and nightlife venues as clients
Deceptive marketing — charts that mislead, testimonials you invent, before/after claims you cannot evidence
Excessive uncertainty in a contract (gharar): vague scope, undefined deliverables, unpriced revisions
prefer: Fee for work done, agreed in writing before you start — scope, price, deliverables, revision count, delivery date
Sectors that are unambiguously clean: government, education, healthcare, infrastructure, energy, manufacturing, non-profits, publishing, halal consumer brands
Products you own and license honestly — templates, themes, courses, books
Profit-and-loss sharing partnerships rather than fixed-interest borrowing, if you ever take investment
practical: A written scope with a fixed price removes most of the uncertainty problem by itself, and it happens to be good business practice too
Keep a simple sector filter in your own pipeline notes, so you decide once rather than case by case under deadline pressure
Zakat applies to business cash and receivables once the year and threshold are met — track them separately from personal money

income.name: Annual and sustainability report design
income.what: Design of annual reports, ESG and sustainability reports for listed companies, government entities and large private groups.
income.whoPays: Corporate communications, investor relations and sustainability teams.
income.howToStart: Rebuild one public report you think is badly designed as a spec piece, show the before and after, and take it to three companies whose current report is worse. Reporting season is annual and predictable, so approach them four months ahead.
income.halalNote: Clean in almost every sector. Check the client's core business — a conventional bank's annual report is a common grey area worth thinking through before you accept.
income.risk: Long approval chains and heavy revision cycles. Price revisions explicitly.

income.name: Dashboard design as a service
income.what: Taking working-but-ugly Power BI reports and rebuilding them so executives can actually read them — layout, hierarchy, colour, chart choice, theme files.
income.whoPays: Analytics teams, BI consultancies, and finance functions who have a developer but no designer.
income.howToStart: This is the rarest combination you own. Publish two teardown case studies — original, problems named, rebuild — and send them to BI consultancies rather than end clients. They resell you.
income.halalNote: Clean. Take care only if the underlying data serves a haram product line.
income.risk: Clients may expect you to also build the data model. Decide where your scope ends and write it down.

income.name: Arabic–Latin bilingual brand systems
income.what: Identity systems that work properly in both scripts — matched type pairing, mirrored layouts, bilingual lock-ups and guidelines.
income.whoPays: GCC government entities, cultural institutions, regional groups, and international brands entering the Gulf.
income.howToStart: Most global studios do this badly and most local work is under-documented. Build a genuine specialism: study Khatt Foundation and regional foundries, then produce one exemplary bilingual guideline as a portfolio piece.
income.risk: Requires real Arabic typographic literacy. Do not fake it — partner with an Arabic type specialist at first.

income.name: Executive presentation systems
income.what: Master template systems for consultancies, boards and executive teams — not one-off decks, but a governed slide library with rules.
income.whoPays: Consultancies, PMOs, C-suite offices, investor relations.
income.howToStart: Sell the system, not the deck. One template that survives 200 users is worth more than 20 decks, and it renews annually as the brand shifts.
income.halalNote: Clean. Watch for fundraising decks with misleading projections — you are responsible for what you help present.
income.risk: Scope creep into endless deck production. Sell training and a rulebook so they can serve themselves.

income.name: Template and asset products
income.what: InDesign report templates, Power BI theme files, chart component libraries, presentation systems, icon sets — sold repeatedly.
income.howToStart: Productise something you have already built for a client, stripped of their brand. Sell on your own site plus one marketplace. The first product teaches you the packaging; the fifth makes the money.
income.halalNote: Clean, provided the licence terms are clear and honest and the assets are genuinely yours.
income.risk: Support burden and piracy. Price for the support, not the file.

income.name: Teaching — a cohort course of your own
income.what: A paid short course on the thing you can teach that few others can: designing dashboards and reports that executives read.
income.whoPays: Analysts who cannot design, designers who cannot chart, and corporate L&D budgets.
income.howToStart: Teach it free once inside your own organisation, record what confuses people, then run it as a paid four-week cohort. Corporate L&D pays far more than individuals.
income.halalNote: Clean, and among the most rewarded forms of income in the tradition — beneficial knowledge that keeps giving.
income.risk: Cohorts are demanding to run live. Start with one small cohort, not a launch.

income.name: In-house corporate training
income.what: Half-day and one-day workshops delivered on site: chart literacy for analysts, brand compliance for marketing teams, report standards for comms.
income.whoPays: HR and L&D budgets, which are separate from project budgets and often easier to access.
income.howToStart: Package three fixed workshops with fixed prices and outcomes. Sell to organisations you already have a relationship with — the first one is a referral, not a cold sale.
income.risk: Travel and scheduling. Price a day rate, not an hourly one.

income.name: AI-accelerated production work
income.what: Volume creative production — campaign adaptations, localisation, image variants, motion cutdowns — delivered faster because you use AI tooling properly.
income.whoPays: Agencies and in-house teams with more output than capacity.
income.howToStart: Sell throughput and consistency, not novelty. Publish your process for keeping brand fidelity across generated assets. Disclose AI use in writing — clients increasingly require it.
income.halalNote: Clean in itself. Be honest about what is generated, respect other people's copyright, and refuse work that fabricates people or events.
income.risk: Rates fall as tools spread. The durable part is your judgment and QC, so sell that.

income.name: Book and publication design
income.what: Interiors, covers, typesetting and print-ready files for publishers, institutions and serious self-publishers.
income.whoPays: Regional publishers, universities, museums, foundations, authors.
income.howToStart: Build a portfolio of interiors, not just covers — that is what separates a book designer from a graphic designer. Institutional publishers pay far better than individual authors.
income.halalNote: Clean. Screen content the same way you screen clients.
income.risk: Individual authors have small budgets and large emotions. Prefer institutions.

income.name: Wayfinding and environmental graphics
income.what: Signage systems, donor walls, exhibition graphics and environmental branding for buildings and developments.
income.whoPays: Developers, architects, facilities and cultural institutions — a large and continuous market in the Gulf.
income.howToStart: Architects are the gatekeepers. One well-documented bilingual signage system opens the category. Learn the fabrication constraints before you pitch.
income.risk: Long project cycles, fabrication liability, site coordination. Contract carefully.

income.name: Writing and documentation
income.what: Technical writing, brand guideline authorship, design system documentation and case-study writing — using the writing half of your skill set.
income.whoPays: Companies with a design system nobody can follow, or a brand nobody understands.
income.howToStart: Most guidelines fail because a designer wrote pictures and no sentences. You do both. Offer 'guideline rescue' as a fixed-price product.
income.risk: Underpriced if sold as 'writing'. Sell it as governance.

ventures.name: A specialist report and disclosure studio
ventures.thesis: ESG and sustainability disclosure is becoming mandatory across more jurisdictions, and most of those documents are designed badly by generalists. A studio that does only reports, and knows the reporting frameworks, can charge like a consultancy.
ventures.firstMove: Pick one framework, learn it properly, and become the designer who understands what the content has to contain — not just how it should look.
ventures.moat: Framework literacy plus repeatable templates. Very few designers have both.
ventures.halalNote: Clean, subject to normal client screening.

ventures.name: A dashboard design practice
ventures.thesis: Every organisation now has BI developers and no designer. The gap between a working report and a readable one is a service nobody is reliably selling.
ventures.firstMove: Partner with two BI consultancies as their white-label design arm before you ever sell direct.
ventures.moat: You sit between two professions that rarely overlap.

ventures.name: A template and systems product business
ventures.thesis: One good report template or Power BI theme sold a thousand times outperforms a hundred bespoke jobs, and it earns while you sleep.
ventures.firstMove: Ship one product. Measure whether anyone buys it before building a catalogue.
ventures.moat: Craft quality and documentation — most templates on the market are visually weak and undocumented.

ventures.name: A regional design publication or newsletter
ventures.thesis: There is no strong, consistently published English-language design publication focused on GCC creative work. Attention in a defined niche converts into consulting, teaching and sponsorship.
ventures.firstMove: Publish weekly for six months before monetising anything. The archive is the asset.
ventures.moat: Consistency. Almost everyone quits before month four.
ventures.halalNote: Clean; keep sponsorships clearly labelled and screen sponsors the same way you screen clients.

ventures.name: Bilingual type and brand tooling
ventures.thesis: Bilingual lock-ups, grids and guideline templates are re-invented badly on every Gulf project. A well-made toolkit would sell to studios across the region.
ventures.firstMove: Build it for your own next bilingual project, then generalise it.
ventures.moat: Genuine bilingual typographic competence is scarce.

ventures.name: Visual standards consulting
ventures.thesis: Large organisations produce thousands of documents a year with no visual standard. Setting that standard — and training people in it — is a governance service, priced like consulting rather than design.
ventures.firstMove: Get IBCS certified, then sell an audit: take fifty of a client's existing reports and show what is inconsistent and what it costs them.
ventures.moat: An audit is a diagnosis. Diagnoses lead to long engagements.

ventures.name: A teaching business
ventures.thesis: You have a rare combination — design craft, data visualisation, technical writing. Very few people can teach all three, and corporate training budgets are large.
ventures.firstMove: One recorded course, one live cohort, one corporate workshop. See which of the three earns most per hour of your time, then do more of it.
ventures.moat: Practitioner credibility. You teach what you shipped last month.
ventures.halalNote: Clean, and durable — teaching keeps returning long after the work is done.

ventures.name: A small studio built around AI throughput
ventures.thesis: A two-or-three person studio using AI tooling well can now deliver what used to need eight people. The advantage is temporary but real, and it funds the next thing.
ventures.firstMove: Do not announce it as an AI studio. Win on speed, price and consistency, and let clients notice.
ventures.moat: Process and quality control, not the tools themselves.
ventures.halalNote: Clean, with honest disclosure of AI use and respect for others' copyright.
